title: Donald Trump is sent to hospital for ‘a series of mini-strokes'
description_short: Donald Trump is sent to hospital for ‘a series of mini-strokes'
description_medium: On November 16, 2019, Trump made an unscheduled visit to Walter Reed National Military Medical Center. He later said the visit was the first part of his annual physical. The supplied account includes no medical record or verified diagnosis supporting the headline’s claim that he had mini-strokes.

title: Trump group urges PA voters to send in ballots after Election Day
description_short: Trump group urges PA voters to send in ballots after Election Day
description_medium: On Election Day, November 3, 2020, Kenosha For Trump, a Wisconsin group connected to Trump Victory, recruited volunteers to contact Trump supporters in Pennsylvania and urge them to send ballots later in the week. Election lawyers said the advice appeared to conflict with state law. The supplied account does not say how many voters were contacted or what happened to any ballots.
description_long: The supplied timeline reports that Kenosha For Trump, a Wisconsin group connected to Trump Victory, enlisted volunteers on November 3, 2020, to contact Trump supporters in Pennsylvania. The volunteers urged voters to send in ballots during the rest of the week, after Election Day. Election lawyers cited in the account said the request appeared to violate Pennsylvania law governing when ballots could be received. The report does not establish that any voter followed the instruction, how many people received the message, or whether any late ballot was accepted or counted. It also does not identify an enforcement action or court ruling resulting from the outreach. The documented event is the group’s reported instruction and the legal concern it raised, not a finding that the group committed a crime or changed the result. Because the outreach involved a Trump-connected volunteer operation and a contested ballot deadline, the episode bears on campaign conduct and election administration. Its practical reach and consequences remain unknown from the supplied record, so they should not be inferred from the instruction alone.

title: Trump: Mike Pompeo and Netanyahu meet with Mohammed Bin Salman in Saudi Arabia
description_short: Trump: Mike Pompeo and Netanyahu meet with Mohammed Bin Salman in Saudi Arabia
description_medium: Reports said Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met in Saudi Arabia on November 22, 2020. Israeli media also reported Mossad chief Yossi Cohen attended, while Saudi officials denied Netanyahu’s presence. The supplied accounts do not establish the agenda, agreements or outcome.
description_long: Reports in November 2020 described a meeting in Saudi Arabia between U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Israeli media said Mossad director Yossi Cohen also attended, and an Israeli cabinet member reportedly disclosed Netanyahu’s presence; Saudi Arabia denied that the meeting had occurred. The conflicting accounts leave the attendance itself disputed in public reporting. The encounter drew attention because Israel and Saudi Arabia did not have formal diplomatic relations at the time, and the reported participants held senior roles in governments with overlapping regional interests. The available account says an Israeli cabinet was briefed afterward but does not provide a transcript, agenda, negotiated terms or confirmation of an agreement. It therefore supports describing a reported high-level encounter and the disagreement over its disclosure, not claiming that the countries reached a deal or normalized relations. Pompeo’s participation connects the event to the Trump administration, but the supplied sources do not document Trump’s role in arranging the meeting or any specific direction he gave.
